name: Replaceable Production Envelope
summary: Keep Agent behavior target-independent while configuration, secrets, telemetry, deployment and rollback remain separately owned replaceable contracts.
context: One Agent must move through local, staging and one or more production targets.
Promotion and rollback need more evidence than a successful deploy command.
forces: Typed lifecycle metadata costs more than one manifest but clarifies ownership.
Strict drift detection interrupts convenient imperative changes.
Rollback actions differ across platform capabilities.
decision: Separate Agent contract, behavior gate, runtime config, secret refs, deployment spec and release record.
Promote the exact immutable artifact and behavior report tested in staging.
Standardize release evidence while keeping target-native rollback execution.
implementation: Render target-independent Agent and behavior artifacts separately from target overlays.
Reject secret material in plain environment configuration and unmanaged live drift.
Govern trace content and full prompt-response capture as separate sinks.
Append source, artifact, spec, eval, platform and previous-release evidence after deployment.

observable_contract.statement: Changing deployment target leaves Agent source and behavior-gate artifacts byte-equivalent.
Remote config contains secret references rather than material and blocks unmanaged live drift.
Trace content and full prompt-response capture have independent approval, sink and retention policy.
Production points to the tested artifact, behavior report, prior release and target-specific rollback action.

failure_modes.statement: A secret is copied through .env as ordinary configuration even if command output is redacted.
Merge-style update preserves an out-of-band runtime value without reviewed desired state.
Mutable current-resource metadata is mistaken for immutable artifact, promotion and rollback history.
One generic rollback command hides a target that only supports restore and redeploy.

counterexamples.context: A disposable local tutorial has no remote users, retained state or release lifecycle.
counterexamples.preferred: Use the minimal local run path without a production release ledger.

counterexamples.context: Targets have materially different deployment capabilities.
counterexamples.preferred: Share evidence and policy but keep separate target-native adapters.

adk_versions.notes: Manifest, scaffold, deploy, metadata and observability source contracts were compared with the offline envelope.
Maintenance-mode template composition and generated CI remain rendered-project lifecycle evidence.

source_evidence.claim: Current scaffold composes shared, language, target and Agent overlays.
Deploy utilities copy project .env, apply explicit precedence and redact displayed Cloud Run commands.
Agent Runtime update preserves unspecified live plain environment values.
Mutable local metadata stores one pending operation or current resource and treats corruption as empty.
Rollback differs among Cloud Run traffic shift, GKE rollout undo and Agent Runtime redeploy.
Trace content and full prompt-response completion uploads are separate telemetry paths.

lab_evidence.claim: Local, Cloud Run and Agent Runtime retain identical Agent and behavior artifacts with bounded target diffs.
Tests block plaintext secrets, full-content telemetry, target mismatch and preserved live drift.
Tests enforce staging promotion, previous release history and target-specific rollback plans.

rejected_decisions.decision: Treat a successful deploy and current resource ID as sufficient promotion and rollback evidence.
rejected_decisions.reason: They do not identify immutable source, artifact, behavior report, prior release or recovery action.
rejected_decisions.replacement: Append immutable release evidence and generate a target-native rollback plan.
